name: The machinery of rule
note: Twelve conditional events — fired by the world, not the calendar. Each declares its condition against live state; if the condition never comes true in a campaign, the event honestly never happens.

events.title: Lending against coin begins in the market towns
events.evidence: The Pali canon's debt vocabulary and the earliest usury discussions, which presuppose coined money.
events.note: Fires only after coinage exists in this campaign — debt at interest needs a unit.

events.title: Contracts move from witnesses to writing
events.evidence: The dharmasutra provisions on documents versus witnesses, and the earliest deed formulae.
events.note: Needs both writing in use and money to count in.

events.title: The nigama: market towns incorporate
events.evidence: Nigama coin legends and seals, which are towns speaking as corporate persons.

events.title: Guilds begin taking deposits at interest
events.evidence: The shreni-nigama banking references, and the later cave inscriptions recording endowments held at interest.
events.note: The perpetual endowment's precondition: an institution that outlives the depositor.

events.title: The copying workshop becomes a standing institution
events.evidence: The jump in recension stability once professional copying begins.
events.note: Fires when five works exist in writing — a scriptorium needs a shelf.

events.title: Administration moves its daily records to paper
events.evidence: The survival curve of routine documents, which steepens an order of magnitude after paper.
events.note: Conditional on paper actually existing in this campaign's world.

events.title: Private libraries multiply beyond courts and temples
events.evidence: The manuscript colophons naming merchant and household owners in growing numbers.

events.title: The royal workshops organise craft production at scale
events.evidence: The karkhana accounts in the Sultanate sources, thousands of artisans on the state's books.

events.title: Persian becomes the language of record beyond the court
events.evidence: The spread of Persian documentary conventions into provincial and eventually Maratha and Rajput chanceries.

events.title: The sarai network makes the trunk roads bankable
events.evidence: The kos minars and sarai chains, and the insurance rates that fell with them.

events.title: The hundi clears across the subcontinent
events.evidence: Bills drawn in Surat and honoured in Murshidabad; the discount rates the firms' ledgers record.
events.note: No single ruler makes this happen — it fires when trade and trust are both deep enough.

events.title: Job printing reaches the district towns
events.evidence: The provincial press registers: wedding invitations, almanacs, caste-association tracts.
